# Cyrus Model Studio: plan (design only, 2026-10-10)

Labels: **V** = I read it in code (cyrus-r2 `lib/cyrus`, cyrus-r13 `assets3d/manifest.ts`, `adapters/asset-profile.ts`, `jobs/asset-jobs.ts`). **U** = unverified. Every quality claim about AI output is **U until a paid eval runs**. Mockups: `*.html` + `shots/` in this folder.

## 1. What exists today (V)
| Piece | Where | Fact that matters here |
|---|---|---|
| RigSpec v1 | `creature/spec.ts` | Zod `strictObject`; bones/cubes/clips; caps 32 bones, 64 cubes, 8 clips, 48 KB; model never writes UVs |
| Compiler | `creature/compile.ts` | box UV `boxFaces` + shelf `layoutSkin` (64/128), deterministic `.bbmodel` (rig-c1) |
| Preview | `creature/preview.ts` | pure software rasteriser, byte-stable PNG |
| Item states | `itemmodel/*` | 8 display contexts, per-category transforms, states; gun transform U in client |
| Texture Studio | `studios/paint.ts`, `editor.ts`, `service.ts` | `TextureDoc` = locked spec + sparse paint layer; `History<T>` 200 steps; save = new revision + asset row, `expectedHeadId` → 409 `stale_head` |
| Gate | `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` | `ASSET_MIN_PLAN.model = "all"`; only create/edit gated; unknown plan fails closed |
| Foundation (r13) | `assets3d/manifest.ts`, `asset-profile.ts`, `asset-jobs.ts` | glTF + sidecar, legal ledger, `libraryEligible`, `WORKER_CLASSES`, in-memory queue + object store (no DB tables yet) |

## 2. Architecture per layer
| Layer | Serves | Canonical data | Human edits | Runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 viewport + paint | every model | `ModelDoc` + `TextureDoc` per texture (reused) | paint, fill face, pick, decals | three.js (MIT) client, lazy route chunk |
| L2 cuboid + bone editor | MC creatures (RigSpec), MC 3D items (`ItemCuboidSpec`), Hytale | RigSpec v1.1 / ItemCuboidSpec v1 | cubes, bones, pivots, UV boxes, keys | client ops on the spec; compile server-side |
| L3 retexture + light edit | FiveM/RedM liveries, later GMod/Zomboid, Palworld/ARK | glTF 2.0 + sidecar, per-channel lossless layers | layers, decal transforms, material values, small transforms | client; unwrap/convert/pack on workers |
| L4 AI mesh | hard-surface and organic props | glTF + sidecar (`ai-mesh`) | transform, material, UV tweaks only (no sculpting) | `linux-cpu` Blender or `gpu` worker |

### Data model additions (Cyrus-prefixed, opaque ids, no FKs into Nxeon)
| Addition | Shape | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ModelDoc` v1 (asset row, kind `model`, mime `application/vnd.cyrus.modeldoc+json`) | `{v, kind: creature\|item3d\|mesh, spec, ids, textures: {key: TextureDoc}, layers, pins}` | one saveable unit; spec stays the build-service contract |
| RigSpec **v1.1** (additive) | optional cube `id`, `uv: [u,v]` pin, `skin.paint` ref | stable ids for merge; pinned UV keeps paint in place. Needs compiler rig-c2 + regenerated build-service copy (strict schema rejects new keys) |
| `ItemCuboidSpec` v1 (new) | elements from/to, single-axis rotation, per-face UV auto/pinned, materials, decal layers; links `ItemModelSpec` states | the real 3D gun; emits one model JSON per state into the existing pack |
| `CyrusModelDraft` | `projectId, ownerRef, assetKey, baseAssetId, baseHeadId, doc, updatedAt`, unique per owner+key | autosave, not a revision |
| `CyrusAssetJob`, `CyrusObject` | DB backing for r13 `JobQueue` / `ObjectStore` | workers, previews, exports |
| `CyrusPreviewRender` | key = sha(specSha + renderer + preset) → object key | cache |
| `CyrusLibraryAsset`, `CyrusLibraryReport` | `assetSha, kind, creatorRef, state, filters Json, legalClass, licenceVersion` | community asset library (today's `CyrusLibraryItem` is a mod-page bookmark, a different thing) |
| `AssetProfile.meshBudget` (proposed) | `{maxTriangles, lods: number[], maxMaterials}` | L4 cleanup target and checks |
| manifest `provenance.generator` (proposed) | `"ai-mesh" \| "ai-spec" \| "studio" \| …` | flags AI-mesh output; library + filters read it |

### Save, revisions, undo, autosave, AI edits
| Concern | Design |
|---|---|
| Undo/redo | client op log on the `ModelDoc`; reuse `History<T>` (200 steps); one gizmo drag / stroke / accepted candidate = one step |
| Autosave | debounce 5 s idle, max 30 s, to `CyrusModelDraft`; reload restores; drafts are never built or shared |
| Save | explicit "Save revision": validate (spec + quality) → compile → revision kind `asset` + asset row; `expectedHeadId` → 409 stale_head, same as textures |
| AI edit mid-session | AI never touches the working copy. It returns a candidate built from base revision R. If the user has unsaved edits: 3-way merge per node id (bone, cube, key, layer); disjoint changes merge, overlaps listed ("1 overlap"); human wins by default; Apply / Apply part / Reject (mockup b) |
| AI writes, human fixes | prompt → spec (never raw mesh, never UVs) → deterministic render + look check → user opens it and fixes; each save is a revision (mockup f) |

## 3. L2 editor operations (cut line for v1)
| v1 | Later |
|---|---|
| select (click, outliner), add/delete/duplicate cube and bone, reparent (drag) | box/lasso multi-select |
| move/resize cube (gizmo + fields, 1/16 snap), inflate | free rotation for items (if version allows, U) |
| bone pivot move, bone rotation, tag none/head/glow | IK, constraints (never: new rigging tools) |
| mirror X (paired `_l/_r`), material + solid/fade | per-face UV editing beyond box UV |
| UV: auto-pack / pinned, show net on the sheet | UV pack optimiser |
| clips: the 5 required + up to 8, keys (rotation, position, scale), linear/smooth, wave tracks, scrub, play, loop | onion skin, curve editor |
| budgets live (RigSpec caps), validator issues inline | |
| decals on faces (existing `DecalZ` ops) | |

## 4. Viewport requirements
| Requirement | Target |
|---|---|
| Channels | profile-aware: Lit, Albedo, Normal, Rough, Metal, AO, Emissive, UV checker, Wire. Channels a profile cannot ship are shown disabled with the reason (MC Java item: albedo only) |
| In-hand / contexts | the 6 `PREVIEW_CONTEXTS` + state scrubber from `ItemModelSpec`, using the pack's own display numbers (fixes the gun-not-in-hand bug: grip anchor check `grip_in_hand`) |
| Performance budget | 60 fps desktop for ≤ 64 cubes; L3/L4 ≤ 150k tris in view, ≤ 4 × 2048² channel textures, GPU memory ≤ 512 MB; stroke-to-pixel ≤ 16 ms at 2048²; three.js chunk lazy-loaded only on studio routes |
| Mobile (< 760 px) | read-only orbit + Approve/Reject; DPR capped 1.5; falls back to the server turntable PNG if WebGL fails |

## 5. Server-side preview render (node-2)
| Lane | How | Determinism |
|---|---|---|
| Cuboid (L1/L2, all MC + Hytale) | extend `creature/preview.ts` software rasteriser (no GPU, pure TS) | byte-identical; golden **hashes** |
| Mesh/PBR (L3/L4) | headless Chromium (Playwright already on node-2) + three.js on SwiftShader, fixed camera presets, DPR 1, no clocks, fixed tone mapping | pinned Chromium build; golden **images** with tolerance (≤ 0.5 % pixels off by > 2/255) |
Runs as `linux-cpu` jobs in the capped `nxeon-build-agents.slice` (2 GB, 200 % CPU, 60 s timeout, no network), same pattern as the sound render host. Never on the primary. Output: 6 context shots + 8-angle turntable, cached by key.

## 6. Hytale `.blockymodel` emitter
New emitter from RigSpec v1.1, behind the Hytale adapter `maturity: experimental`; export unlocks per item only after a real client loads it (mockup d). **All U** (from memory and host wikis, not official docs): node/shape schema (box vs quad, offset vs position, stretch); per-face `textureLayout` (offset, mirror, angle); units, pivot origin, quaternion orientation; `.blockyanim` keyframe format vs our 5 baked clips; texture size rules; asset pack `manifest.json` and server streaming handshake; Linux dedicated server availability. Keep it a pure function with versioned fixtures so a format change is one file.

## 7. L4: AI mesh generation (owner addition)
| Route | How | Quality / cost (all U) |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Script geometry | Claude writes Blender-Python (bmesh, modifiers, bevels, booleans) run headless in a sandboxed `linux-cpu` worker (no network, allow-listed modules, 10 min cap); render 6 views → vision model compares to the prompt → Claude revises the script, max 4 passes | best for hard-surface (guns, crates, lanterns); token cost per pass unknown; organic shapes weak |
| (b) Parts library | Cyrus-owned kits (receiver, barrel, stock, grip, magazine; wheels, cabins) assembled by script with sockets | the main quality lever; needs authoring time; parts are `platform-library` class |
| (c) Image/text-to-3D | self-hosted TRELLIS (MIT) on a `gpu` worker; Meshy/Tripo only with owner spend approval; Hunyuan3D excluded (licence excludes EU/UK/KR) | blobby topology, no rig, unknown UVs; always goes through cleanup |
| Cleanup (all routes) | decimate/retopo to `meshBudget.maxTriangles`; xatlas UV; bake normal (and AO) from the high-poly; LOD chain per `meshBudget.lods`; manifold, watertight, UV-overlap, scale/units checks | fails closed: an asset that misses budget or checks is not saved |
Lands in: `AssetProfile.meshBudget`, manifest `provenance.generator: "ai-mesh"`, legal class `ai-generated-for-user`. Human step stays: transform, material values, UV tweaks in Model Studio, never sculpting (mockup a, `?mesh=1`). Not for Minecraft Java (no meshes); useful for FiveM props and later UE games.

## 8. What Claude can and cannot produce (say this in the product)
| Layer | Realistic | Not |
|---|---|---|
| L2 | blocky items, creatures, props for MC and Hytale | smooth/organic shapes |
| L1 | paint, stickers, decals, wear | photo-real textures |
| L3 | realistic vehicles/clothing **only** as a retexture of a template the user supplies | new realistic meshes, anything shipping the base mesh |
| L4 | stylised or simple hard-surface props within a budget | rigged characters, hero assets, guaranteed likeness |
Quality for every row is unverified until the paid eval (100 owner-labelled samples, the existing vision-judge plan).

## 9. Community asset library (owner decisions: automatic, not opt-in)
- **Flow:** asset saved → if `libraryEligible(manifest)` → `pending checks` → filters → `published` or `held for review` → (report) → `removed`. States shown as badges in the studio and "My contributions" (mockup e).
- **Never enters:** game-derived, third-party-licensed, imported. **Gap found (V):** `libraryEligible` only excludes `provenance.source === "import"`; a file the user **uploaded** is `source: "user"` and passes. Add an `uploaded` source (or flag). Also exclude anything whose `derivedFrom` hits a game-derived hash (a livery is only meaningful on the game's mesh).
- **Filters (lib-1):** provenance, trademark/logo (text + vision), real-weapon names (AK-47, Glock... a hold, not a block), adult content (vision on 6 renders), near-copy of known game assets (perceptual hash vs a reference set). All thresholds U.
- **Rights:** licence grant in the Terms of Service at sign-up and repeated in the studio; creator keeps copyright; attribution `@handle` kept in pack credits; report + takedown queue with a person; removal does not break mods already using the asset (U: owner decision).
- **Gate:** browsing open to all; "Use in project" = asset create → follows `canAsset` for the kind (today: model/texture = All models, sound = Saka). The owner's "usable by anyone" conflicts with this; decision needed.

## 10. Plan placement (proposal, owner decides)
Model Studio paint, edit and retexture at **All models** (matches `ASSET_MIN_PLAN.model`). Never gated: view, orbit, in-game preview, install, export, rebuild, Mod Packs, import, library browsing. Server checks every create/edit; unknown plan fails closed for edits only. Alternative: give Saka **paint-only** on existing models (cheap upsell) — it writes textures, so it would contradict the Texture Studio gate.

## 11. Testing
| Level | What |
|---|---|
| Unit | spec v1.1 / ItemCuboidSpec validators, merge (3-way per node), op log undo/redo, UV pin + resample, budgets, gate per op, `libraryEligible` cases |
| Golden | cuboid renderer hashes per fixture; mesh lane image diffs; compiler output hashes (`.bbmodel`, item JSON per state, `.blockymodel`) |
| Integration | save → revision → pack, workers on the memory queue, stale_head + overlap paths |
| Real Test Flight | MC 26.x: BetterModel creature load + item states in hand (player client, owner) |
| Stays unverified without a real client | Hytale everything; FiveM YTD in-game; GMod VTF; gun display transforms until a person looks; vision-judge scores |

## 12. Phased tasks (size, model)
| # | Task | Size | Model | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | DB tables for jobs/objects/drafts/preview cache + host seam wiring | M | Sonnet | r13 |
| F2 | `ModelDoc` + RigSpec v1.1 + rig-c2 + regenerated service copy | M | Opus | F1 |
| F3 | ItemCuboidSpec v1 + emitter into the pack + states | L | Opus | F2 |
| F4 | Cuboid preview lane on node-2 (jobs, cache, contexts, turntable) | M | Sonnet | F1 |
| L1a | three.js viewport shell, orbit, channels, contexts/state scrubber | L | Opus | F2 |
| L1b | paint-on-model (raycast → texel → TextureDoc), decals, UV panel | M | Opus | L1a |
| L2a | editor ops v1 + gizmo + outliner + op log + autosave | L | Opus | L1a |
| L2b | timeline + keys + clip validation | M | Opus | L2a |
| L2c | candidate 3-way merge UI | M | Opus | L2a |
| H1 | `.blockymodel` emitter behind maturity flag + fixtures | M | Sonnet | F2 |
| L3a | glTF import, sidecar, legal class, job retention, channel layers | L | Opus | F1 |
| L3b | UV island view, layer transforms, export picker; mesh preview lane | M | Sonnet | L3a |
| L3c | FiveM YTD packing on the Windows worker | L | Opus | L3a + worker |
| L4a | Blender script worker + look loop + cleanup pipeline + meshBudget | L | Opus | F1, paid eval |
| LIB | library tables, filters, states, report/takedown, My contributions | L | Opus (filters) / Sonnet (UI) | F1, ToS |
| QA | golden suites, Test Flight scripts | M | Sonnet | each |
Order: F1 → F2 → (F3, F4, L1a) → L1b → L2a → L2b/L2c → H1 → L3a → L3b → L3c → L4a; LIB can start after F1 once the ToS text exists.

## 13. Owner decisions
1. Plan placement (section 10), and whether Saka gets paint-only.
2. Library "usable by anyone" vs the plan gate on "Use in project".
3. Library: does removal pull the asset from mods already using it?
4. Real-weapon names: hold for review (proposed) or block; allowed in private mods (proposed yes).
5. L4 spend: paid eval budget; Meshy/Tripo API use; a GPU worker at all.
6. Hytale emitter now (experimental) or after a real client is available.
7. L3 template retention: session only (proposed) vs a short encrypted cache (legal call).
8. ToS licence wording (needs a lawyer); AI-output copyright position per region.

## 14. Honest risks
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Paint lost when a painted cube is resized/relaid | UV pin + nearest resample + warning |
| RigSpec schema bump breaks the build service copy | additive v1.1, generated copy, test checks both |
| Display transforms for guns unverified | `grip_in_hand` check + one owner Test Flight before launch |
| Hytale format churn | experimental flag, export gated on real-client check |
| AI mesh quality below "not cheap" bar | parts library first, budget/cleanup fail closed, paid eval before marketing |
| Community library legal exposure (trademarks, real guns, near-copies, AI copyright) | filters + hold + takedown; lawyer on ToS before launch |
# Cyrus Model Studio v3: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files (self-contained, no network): `viewport-paint.html` (a; `?mesh=1` = Layer 4 AI-mesh state), `model-editor.html` (b), `retexture.html` (c), `locked-states.html` (d; `?state=unknown|experimental`), `library.html` (e; `?tab=mine`), `prompt-flow.html` (f). Sources `src/` (v2 kit + `ms.css`, `ms.js`, `m3d.js`, `models.js`), build `tools/build.py`, shots `tools/run-shots.sh` (node-2, capped slice) → `shots/` (28 PNGs: dark, light and 390 px narrow for each). `ctl=0` hides the mockup bar.

## Principles
- **Same product as v2.** Shipped portal shell, Cyrus bar with a Texture / Sound / **Model** switch, glass panels, inspector tabs, prompt dock, narrow approve view.
- **Real geometry, not pictures.** `m3d.js` is a small deterministic canvas renderer standing in for three.js: orbit, picking, channel views, wireframe, affine-mapped textures. Painting writes real texels; the timeline scrubs a real pose; livery layer toggles rebuild every channel.
- **One accent.** Violet = selected/primary. Cyan = "now" (timeline playhead) only. Green/amber/red = pass/warn/fail. One exception: gizmo and axis triad use muted X/Y/Z red/green/blue, the 3D convention people expect.
- **Profile-aware truth.** Channels a game cannot ship are disabled with the reason (Minecraft Java item: albedo only). Delivery status per export target (FiveM "planned": the Windows worker is not built). Hytale shows its unverified format list. "Not run" is never a pass.
- **Legal class is visible.** Game-derived templates carry an amber badge, "kept for this session only, never shared", and ship delta-only. The library shows provenance, attribution and every check.

## Screens → data
| Screen | Data |
|---|---|
| a Paint | `ItemCuboidSpec` draft of `glock_9mm` (9 elements, 22.5° grip), `TextureDoc` paint layer (51 px "worn edge"), `ItemModelSpec` contexts (6) + states (idle/aim/reload; reload slides the slide back), checks incl. `grip_in_hand` |
| a `?mesh=1` | L4 output: LOD0-3 vs `meshBudget` (sample numbers), materials as lossless channel layers, cleanup checks, provenance `ai-mesh` |
| b Editor | RigSpec `banshee` (8 bones, 12 cubes, 5 clips), live budgets vs real caps, box-UV net on the 128 sheet with Auto-pack / Pinned, candidate bar with "1 overlap" (3-way merge) |
| c Retexture | glTF template stand-in (8,788 tris, 7 slots), body_paint layers with albedo/rough/metal values, UV island view, export picker with delivery status, policy row from the adapter legal block |
| d Locked | `canAsset(plan, "model", "edit")` strings verbatim; plan matrix with the proposed rows marked; Hytale maturity flag |
| e Library | automatic contribution: states pending checks / in the library / held for review / removed / not shared; lib-1 filters; `libraryEligible` exclusions |
| f Prompt flow | "AK-47 with fire stickers" → L2 + L1 route → ItemCuboidSpec + decal layer → deterministic render (sha) + look check → hand fixes as revisions → library "held" (real-weapon name) |

## Component inventory (React)
`ModelViewport`, `ChannelSwitch`, `ToolRail`, `GizmoLayer`, `InGamePreview`, `UvTexturePanel`, `Outliner`, `BudgetPanel`, `TransformFields`, `UvBoxField`, `Timeline`, `CandidateBar`, `MaterialSlots`, `ChannelLayerList`, `UvIslandView`, `ExportTargets`, `LegalClassBadge`, `PolicyCard`, `PolyBudget`, `LibraryGrid`, `LibraryDetail`, `ContributionTable`, `LibraryStateBadge`, `PromptFlow`; reuse `StudioLock` and `PlanMatrix`.

## Interaction details
- Left drag on the model = tool (paint/select); right drag or empty space = orbit; wheel = zoom. B/E/G/I paint tools; Q/W/E/R/P select/move/rotate/resize/pivot; X mirror; Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z.
- Every stroke, drag, key or accepted candidate is one undo step; drafts autosave; "Save revision" is explicit.
- Narrow: turntable, what changed, checks, Approve / Reject; locked plans get view-only with no approve.

## Honesty notes
Sample content is labelled; poly counts, look-check scores and filter results are illustrative. The mockup renderer is not the production renderer (three.js) and the lantern proxy is lower-poly than its LOD1 readout. Gun display transforms, element rotation rules per version, everything Hytale, RAGE normal convention and every AI quality claim are unverified.

## Questions for the owner
1. **Plan:** Model Studio at All models (matches today's gate), or paint-only for Saka?
2. **Library access:** you said "usable by anyone"; the gate today treats "Use in project" as asset creation (All models for models). Open it to every plan, or keep browse-open / use-gated?
3. **Library removals:** when an asset is removed after a report, do mods already using it keep it?
4. **Real-weapon names** (AK-47, Glock): hold for review in the library (proposed) and allow freely in private mods?
5. **Terms of Service:** the automatic licence grant needs a lawyer's wording; also AI-output copyright per region. Who drafts it?
6. **Uploads gap:** `libraryEligible` lets user uploads through (`source: "user"`). Confirm they must be excluded (I think yes) so the code gets an `uploaded` source.
7. **L4 spend:** budget for the paid quality eval, a GPU worker, and Meshy/Tripo trials?
8. **Hytale:** build the emitter now behind the experimental flag, or wait for a real client to test against?
9. **Retexture templates:** session-only (proposed) is safest but means re-attaching the file each time. Acceptable?
10. Gizmo axis colours as the one accent exception: OK?

# N: Hytale verification (read 2026-10-10)

## Biggest unknowns
1. Full EULA/ToS text on AI-generated content and on a service selling mod creation (summaries only; fetch of ToS blocked).
2. Exact Game Server Provider terms (support pages 403), and whether Nxeon's customers can run servers under Nxeon's licence/entitlement.
3. Hard limits: texture size, model node count, asset-pack size, hot reload.
4. Format churn: weekly pre-releases; no stability guarantee in EA.
5. `.blockymodel` / `.blockyanim` schema not officially published in what we read; derive from a Blockbench plugin source/real files.

## Owner must decide
- Apply for the Game Server Provider (`sessions.unlimited_servers`) account before any Hytale hosting; without it, 100 servers per licence and each customer auth is awkward.
- Read the EULA/ToS personally (AI, resale of generated mods, hosting); only then flip legal.reviewed.
- Accept EA churn: ship Cyrus Hytale as "planned/beta" behind a flag, with a game-version field on every pack.
- Hosting pricing: 4-8 GB RAM, 4+ cores per server is heavier than Minecraft; no Hytale SKU exists yet.
## 3. Architecture needed now

**Canonical asset model (decision):** glTF 2.0 (meshes, UV sets, skeleton, metallic-roughness PBR) plus a Cyrus sidecar manifest (provenance, legal class, per-slot role, units). Alternatives rejected: USD (heavy, no web viewer ecosystem), FBX (proprietary SDK), engine-native formats (lock-in). **Store channels as separate lossless layers** (albedo sRGB, normal, roughness, metallic, AO, emissive, height, masks) and **pack only at export** per engine. Units: metres, +Y up (glTF); the adapter converts axis/handedness.

**Per-engine packing (adapter's job; all U, verify per game before shipping):**

| Target | Typical channel convention |
|---|---|
| Unreal (Palworld, ARK) | BaseColor, Normal (DirectX, -Y), ORM pack (AO/Rough/Metal) |
| Unity (Unturned) | Metallic in R, smoothness in alpha; OpenGL normal |
| Source (GMod) | VTF DXT1/DXT5, `$basetexture`/`$bumpmap`, phong masks |
| GTA/RAGE (FiveM) | Diffuse + normal + spec in YTD (DDS inside RSC container) |
| Fallout 4 | DDS BC7 diffuse, BC5 normal (V: nexusmods Fallout 4 guides via search) |
| Hytale | PNG per model (flat albedo, U) |

**Libraries (licence verified from repo LICENSE/GitHub API on 2026-10-10 unless marked):**

| Need | Pick | Licence | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| BCn encode (Windows worker) | DirectXTex `texconv`, DirectXMesh | MIT (V) | Windows exe, ok in worker |
| BCn/KTX2 on Linux | Basis Universal (UASTC/ETC1S, BC7 transcode) | Apache-2.0 (V) | also web delivery |
| KTX2 tooling | KTX-Software | Apache-2.0 for repo files, third-party mixed (V) | check bundled deps |
| Compressonator | GPUOpen | no licence detected by GitHub (U: MIT in practice) | avoid until checked |
| Mesh optimise/LOD | meshoptimizer | MIT (V) | |
| UV unwrap/atlas | xatlas | MIT (V) | |
| Import/convert | assimp | BSD-style (V header) | |
| glTF processing | glTF-Transform / gltf-pipeline | Apache-2.0 (gltf-pipeline V; glTF-Transform U) | |
| Viewer | three.js | MIT (V) | server-side preview via headless Chromium or a small Node renderer |
| Heavy DCC | Blender headless, **separate process only** | GPL (V "NOASSERTION", GPL in practice U) | glTF-Blender-IO Apache-2.0 (V) |
| Do not embed/ship | Blockbench (GPL-3, V), Sollumz (GPL-3, V), CodeWalker (no licence, V), Crowbar (none found) | | Run only in isolated workers on user data, never redistribute; legal review before CodeWalker use |

**Windows build worker:** one more worker class beside node-2 Linux builds. Ephemeral VM per job (or snapshot revert), no outbound network except the broker, **pull-based** job queue, signed job manifest, allow-listed tools only, hard timeout and CPU/RAM caps, no Proxmox or Nxeon credentials on the guest, outputs returned through object storage and re-scanned on Linux (format validators, size caps, forbidden-content scan). Game installs (Creation Kit, UE dev kits, GTA files) are legal-gated: only if the game's EULA allows hosted use (U for all); default = user supplies templates.

**AI texturing (reality check):**

| Option | Facts | Use |
|---|---|---|
| LLM spec + procedural/deterministic render (existing approach) | cheap, reproducible | default; masks per UV region from adapter |
| Image model into UV space with region masks, then seamless tiling | image models do not understand UVs; works with masks/templates | texture lane |
| PBR estimation | Material Palette (MIT, V search); normals from height and heuristic roughness are deterministic and free | derive channels, do not hallucinate them |
| Meshy / Tripo APIs | paid plans own the output; Meshy free tier is CC BY 4.0 (V: docs.meshy.ai/en/webapp/pricing; tripo3d.ai blog); low-poly modes exist, quality claims are vendor marketing | prototype props only, per-call cost |
| Hunyuan3D-2 | Community licence **excludes EU, UK, South Korea** and forbids using outputs to train other models (V: repo LICENSE) | **NO** |
| TRELLIS | MIT (V api) | optional self-host prop prototypes; still no game-ready topology/UV/rig |

Text-to-3D gives static prop blobs, not game-ready characters or vehicles: no rig, wrong topology, unknown UVs. Do not promise it.

**Storage/jobs:** S3-compatible content-addressed store (sha256 keys), 4K PBR sets run 100+ MB uncompressed so cap per tenant and store derivatives lazily. Jobs get a `workerClass` (`linux-cpu`, `windows-tools`, `gpu`); start API-based for image models, no own GPU cluster.

**Asset-profile contract fields each adapter declares:**
`game, engineFamily, meshFormats[], textureFormats[], compression[] (BC1/3/5/7, PNG), channelMap{role->file/channel}, normalConvention, colorSpace per slot, maxRes/budget per class, uvRules (reuse-template vs new), skeletonPolicy (reuse|none|forbidden), packaging (zip, pak, ytd, gma, asset pack), delivery (server-streamed | workshop-user-publishes | workshop-platform-publishes | client-manual | none), workerClass, requiredGameFiles (none|user-supplied|platform-licensed), legal{ policyUrl, commercialOk, aiOk, redistributeBase:false, monetisationRule, attestationRequired, retrievedAt }, validators[], previewShader, maturity`.

**Legal ledger rule:** every asset row carries a class: `user-original`, `ai-generated-for-user`, `platform-library` (Nxeon-owned/CC0 only), `third-party-licensed`, or `game-derived`. **Game-derived assets are never stored beyond the job, never added to any library, never redistributed**; deliverables must contain only user-original or delta content (a retexture ships the texture, not the base mesh). A per-game policy flag (from the table above, with source URL and date) gates export, commercial sharing and the community library; owner reviews each policy page when it changes.

content.thinking:
I'm planning out the file structure for the editor module, starting with the core document model that will capture the creature's metadata, palette, textures, bone hierarchy, and cube definitions.

Each cube needs origin, size, rotation, pivot, and inflate, plus a UV scheme that can be either auto-packed or pinned per-face, so I'm deciding how to structure that union type and noting that cube-level rotation isn't yet supported by RigSpec v1, which is a potential issue to flag.

For deterministic replay, ids and the per-face UV layout need to derive from a counter stored in the doc rather than randomness, so I'm planning out ids.ts and the op-applying logic that will handle this state.

I'm now enumerating the full operation set the document model needs — cube/bone creation, deletion, duplication, mirroring, transforms with snapping, UV pin/unpin, hierarchy and grouping, plus keyframe and clip operations for animation. I also need to nail down snapping granularity, since Blockbench's 16-units-per-block convention makes "1/16 snap" ambiguous and worth clarifying.

For history, I'm sketching an op log that stores a base document plus a sequence of logged operations, replaying deterministically with periodic snapshots to cap memory, folding old ops into the base once the log exceeds 200 steps, and considering whether to merge consecutive gizmo-drag ops into a single entry.

Then for validate.ts, I'm designing structured issue reporting with code, severity, path, and node references, covering checks like rig limits, name safety, texture path safety, and per-game profile constraints — including flagging unsupported cube rotations for certain rig spec targets.

For rigspec.ts, I need fromRigSpec and toRigSpec to form a clean round trip: converting a spec into editor doc form and back must reproduce the original spec exactly, both in deep equality and byte-stable canonical JSON serialization, with bone pivots, rotations, and cube decals all preserved through editing and saving.

Since RigSpec v1 has no cube rotation field, toRigSpec should fail validation if any cube has non-zero rotation -- I'm weighing whether to auto-wrap rotated cubes into a generated bone (which messes with bone count and animations) versus just surfacing a clear error telling the user to rotate the bone instead, reserving true cube rotation for a future RigSpec v1.1. Similarly, since v1 doesn't store UV pins (the compiler repacks UVs), I need a warning that pinned UVs only persist in the editor doc and get re-packed on RigSpec v1 compile.

For export, I'm chaining toRigSpec, checkRigSpec, and compileCreature together, and making sure doc serialization uses sorted keys for byte-stable output, reusing the canonical JSON helper from the textures module. For pose sampling, I want to reuse the compiler's sampleTrack logic for consistency rather than writing a separate sampler, though I'll need my own small matrix math in the scene module since the viewport needs world matrices from the full EditorDoc (including hidden cubes and cube rotation) rather than just a compiled RigSpec.

Now I'm working through keyframe editing: setKey, removeKey, and moveKey operations need to respect the rule that tracks must start at t=0 and end at t=1, so creating a new track means seeding it with base-value keys at both ends plus the user's actual key. Wave tracks will stay read-only in the timeline for now, with just a "convertWaveToKeys" bake operation that samples 8 points per cycle, capped by the max keys per track limit.

For merge logic, I'm thinking through 3-way merging per node identity — bones, cubes, and keys each need stable ids so I can diff base vs. ours vs. the AI's candidate, with keys identified by their clip, track, and time position.

I also need to handle id and name collisions: if both sides add new nodes, the AI candidate reuses the same id counter as the base, so colliding ids need remapping, and duplicate bone names should get a suffix with a reported warning. Conflicting edits to the same node default to the human side winning, with deletions versus edits always flagged as overlaps.

Since AI-generated RigSpecs lack ids (unless using v1.1's optional cube id), I need to match them against the base doc by bone name and by (bone, cube index) pairs to assign stable ids before merging.

For exporters, I'm designing a game-neutral `ModelExporter` interface with a maturity-aware registry, where "planned" exporters only run under an explicit dev/test flag and otherwise fail with a clear `exporter_planned` error code.

Concretely I'm planning "rigspec-bbmodel" (minecraft, beta) and "hytale-blockymodel" (planned, draft-only), building the Hytale exporter around verified facts—cuboids/quads, .blockymodel/.blockyanim formats, PNG textures, fixed pixel-per-unit scales for blocks vs. mobs/players, and the asset pack folder layout—while marking the actual JSON schema as unverified and tagging it accordingly in the output.

I'm deciding to move the draft notice out of the blockymodel file itself and into a sidecar cyrus-export.json instead, since embedding a draft marker key risks breaking a real loader. I'm sketching an assumed node-based JSON layout from memory of a Blockbench Hytale plugin—boxes with position/orientation, texture layout per face, shading mode, children arrays—but flagging every piece of this structure as unverified, including the unit scale (possibly 32 units per block in Hytale versus my 16-per-block convention).

Working through texture density, I reason that if mobs need 64px per block-unit and my skin is 16px per block, the exporter would need to upscale the skin 4x nearest-neighbor for mobs and 2x for blocks, assuming geometry units stay fixed—labeling "unit = one block" as an assumption to track. I'm now sketching the animation file format, a .blockyanim structure with duration, hold-last-keyframe flag, and per-node position keyframes with time/delta values.

I plan a golden test that exports a fixture model and diffs it against a stored JSON file, documenting assumptions in the test itself since JSON lacks comments. Then I shift to thinking about the model edit gate function, mapping operations like edit, create, view, export, and approve to permission checks, and wondering whether "approve" counts as an edit since it saves a new revision.

I'm now sketching the server save path for models, reusing the StudioStore interface from the studios service, defining the asset kind and MIME type, and working out the save-revision flow through validation, rig-spec conversion, and compilation, along with what manifest entries get produced for the model doc, rig spec, and bbmodel outputs.

content.thinking:
Since compile.ts imports node:crypto, the editor core can't depend on it for client safety, so I'll need my own sampler implementation that mirrors sampleTrack's behavior, plus a test to confirm they stay in sync—or maybe I should look at whether preview.ts is a better place for this.

I'm confirming checkRigSpec from spec.ts is already client-safe since it just uses zod/mini and templates, so validate.ts can call it directly on exports. The rig export via toRigSpec stays pure and client-safe too, while bbmodel export needs to live in a server-only file that uses compileCreature.

Now I'm sketching out the actual data model: defining types for bones (with id, name, parent reference, pivot, rotation, and tags like head/glow), cubes (origin, size, rotation, pivot, inflate, material, shading mode, and texture slot references) to represent the editable document structure.

Still writing data model types...

I'm deciding on ordering conventions -- bones follow RigSpec order, cubes are grouped and ordered within their parent bone, and clips are stored as a record where key order needs to stay canonical for byte-stable JSON output.

I also need to resolve track and key identity. Tracks should be uniquely identified by clip name, bone id, and channel, but giving individual keys their own ids seems unnecessary since it would bloat the schema and the RigSpec candidates don't carry key-level ids anyway.

Keys can match by (clip, bone, channel, t) when importing a candidate against a base doc, which is simpler and good enough for merging. So the plan becomes: 3-way merge per node id (bone, cube, key, layer), where tracks are lists of keys and the merge unit is the key itself, with ids assigned deterministically via traversal order in fromRigSpec, matching against a base document when provided.

Bone names need to stay unique, while cube names aren't part of RigSpec itself—compiled names derive from bone and index, with an optional editor-only label for display purposes that gets dropped on export. Cube rotation and pivot are editor-only unless the export target supports them, so RigSpec v1 should error on nonzero rotation, and pivot should default to the cube's center (origin plus half the size) when rotation is absent.

For coordinates, I'm weighing whether to store from/to directly versus origin+size, since recomputing to = origin+size introduces tiny floating-point errors; rounding to 4 decimal places should still round-trip exactly as long as the original values have four or fewer decimal places, since the error from subtraction and re-addition is far smaller than the rounding threshold.

The snap param rounds resulting positions to a grid while preserving size, and since RigSpec coordinates are absolute, moving a bone must translate the pivot plus all descendant cubes and bones together. For rotation, bones get an absolute or delta rotation with optional degree snapping, while cube rotation stays editor-only for RigSpec v1. For scale, I'm defining how cube resize sets the new dimensions.

I'm also designing a mirror operation across the X axis for bones named with `_l`/`_r` suffixes, duplicating the subtree with negated x-coordinates for pivots and cube bounds, swapped naming, and mirrored rotation (negating y/z) to reflect across that plane.

I'm deciding to error out if the mirrored target name already exists rather than overwrite it, and optionally propagate this to animation tracks by default, copying each bone's keyframes to its mirrored counterpart with negated y/z rotation and x position, skipping bones that already have a track.

For duplicate, I'm planning cube copies to stay in place while bone duplicates get a unique `_2` suffix and copy the whole subtree without animations. Delete removes a cube or a bone's entire subtree plus any referencing tracks, but the root bone is protected from deletion. Reparenting lets a bone move to a new non-descendant parent or a cube move to a new bone, keeping absolute world coordinates unchanged. I'm also sketching out pivot editing and UV-setting operations for cubes.

For UV, I'm thinking through pin/unpin behavior where unpinning all boxes triggers auto-layout, but since the compiler always repacks UVs regardless of pins, I need the editor's auto-mode preview to match the compiler's packing exactly — which means potentially reusing layoutSkin from compile.ts, except that file imports node:crypto, so pulling it into client code would break the Next.js build.

A clean fix would be refactoring layoutSkin out into a shared, client-safe file under creature/ and re-exporting it from compile.ts, but that risks a merge conflict if r16's viewport work needs the same client-safe layout logic and does an identical refactor. I'll go with duplicating the layout algorithm in the editor's uv.ts and adding an equivalence test against compile.layoutSkin to keep them in sync, accepting the duplication as safer than risking conflicting refactors.

Now I'm thinking through other operations: hide/lock via setFlag(ids, hidden|locked, value); grouping, which wraps selected cubes or bones into a new parent bone positioned at the pivot of the selection, requiring all selected items to share a common parent; and renaming rules for bones, cubes, and clips, including uniqueness and format validation plus special handling for required clip names.

For keyframes, I'm defining setKey to insert or replace a key at a given time (treating keys within a tiny epsilon as duplicates), auto-creating tracks with rest-value keys at t=0 and t=1 if none exist, and rejecting attempts to set keys directly on wave tracks until they're converted. I'm also laying out deleteKey (protecting the first/last keys), deleteTrack, setEase, moveKey, convertWave, and clip management operations (addClip, setClip, deleteClip). Now I'm turning to how rest-pose edits should relate to animation data.

For material and structural edits, I'm defining setProps for cubes (material, shade, fadeTo, inflate) and bone tagging, plus addBone and addCube operations — every op explicitly carries its target ids so replay stays deterministic, and failed ops simply aren't logged. For history management, I'm designing an OpLog structure with a base document, an ordered list of entries, a current position, and optional checkpoints, where applying an op appends an entry (truncating redo history) and undo/redo move the position and replay from the base.

I'm capping history at 200 steps by folding the oldest entry into the base when exceeded, and memoizing a doc per step so undo/redo can just index into a cache instead of replaying every time, relying on shallow structural sharing for efficiency. I'm also handling gesture coalescing — like gizmo drags that emit many preview ops — so that a push with a matching coalesce key replaces the previous entry instead of appending a new one.

Actually, composing ops generally is tricky, so it's simpler to keep live drag previews outside the undo log entirely and only commit a single op on release, same for inspector fields committing on blur or enter. That avoids needing coalescing logic at all.

Now I'm sketching out validation: a function that checks a document against a target profile (like RigSpec v1 constraints) and returns a list of issues with severity, path, and node references, starting with structural checks for unique ids, acyclic bone parenting, and valid track-to-bone references.

I'm also outlining naming checks (bone, model, clip regexes, safe texture paths), size and count limits pulled from creature spec constants (max bones, cubes, depth, clips, tracks, keys, coordinate bounds), and target-specific rules — Minecraft disallows cube rotation and treats UV pins/hidden cubes as warnings or info, while hidden cubes still get exported since they're only hidden in the editor view.

From there the authoritative check runs toRigSpec then checkRigSpec, mapping any errors back to node ids with a "rigspec" issue code, and I'm defining a budgets function that reports bones, cubes, depth, clips, tracks, keys, spec bytes, and skin pixel usage for the budget panel. For per-game texture resolution limits I'm using the asset profile's maxTextureRes, with Minecraft capped at 128 and a placeholder draft profile for Hytale at 256 until that spec is finalized.

For the merge logic, I'm comparing base, ours, and theirs across bones, cubes, keys, clips, tracks, and palette entries by their canonical JSON representation: if only theirs changed I take theirs, if only ours changed I keep ours, and if both changed to the same result I treat it as unchanged, otherwise I flag it as an overlap defaulting to "human wins" while recording both versions for manual resolution.

I'm refining granularity so overlaps are meaningful — doing field-level comparison within bones/cubes (so an AI resize and a human material change on the same cube don't falsely collide) while keeping keys compared as whole nodes, and building merged arrays starting from ours' ordering, applying theirs' modifications in place and appending new additions from theirs.

For deletions and orphans, I'm deciding that a deletion conflicting with a modification counts as an overlap defaulting to "ours," and that orphaned cubes/tracks left behind by a bone deletion should get dropped with a reported note. I also need to handle name or id collisions from parallel additions by renaming theirs and flagging it.

Since theirs is generated via fromRigSpec with ids allocated past base.seq, and ours also allocates past base.seq, id collisions are likely, so I need a remap step that reassigns fresh ids to any theirs-only ids before merging. I'm also noting that matching theirs to base by name still works even if ours renamed something, since that matching only involves theirs and base.

Now I'm sketching the applyMerge signature with accept/resolve options and deterministic change ids, then defining the exporter interface — ExportFile, ExportResult, and the ModelExporter contract with id, game, format, maturity, and an export function — plus a server-only exporters registry since formats like bbmodel need node:crypto and Hytale needs PNG encoding.

I'm working through runExport's maturity gate: planned exporters are refused unless allowPlanned is set for dev/test contexts, returning an "exporter_planned" code, while export itself stays ungated by the asset plan system. For the Hytale draft exporter I'm mapping out the output file layout, like blockymodel files and PNG textures for blocks, versus a different folder structure for mobs and characters.

Since the exact creature folder layout isn't verified, I'm settling on a neutral structure per creature with its model, texture, animation clips, and a `cyrus-export.json` sidecar flagging it as a draft with an unverified list. I'm skipping manifest.json since its fields are unclear, and instead listing that as an unverified gap, while sketching out the assumed blockymodel node structure from memory of the Blockbench Hytale plugin.

Still refining node schema...

I'm also figuring out how inflate maps to a stretch factor for shape size, how face names like front/back map to Hytale's north/south/east/west conventions, and how texture pixel density scales relative to Blockbench's standard.

For animation files, I'm sketching the .blockyanim format with keyframed position, orientation, stretch, visibility, and UV offset tracks per node, using frame-based timing at 60fps, and considering baking wave motion into fixed samples per cycle.

Since there's no verified scale channel in the target format, I'll mark scale tracks as dropped and emit a warning rather than silently losing data.

For verification, I'm planning a golden test using a floating_ghost fixture, exporting it and comparing the resulting JSON and PNG hash against checked-in golden files, including documenting any unverified assumptions explicitly in the test itself.

Now I'm defining the gate logic in gate.ts: mapping editor actions (view, export, approve, save, autosave, ai_edit, create) onto asset operations, where edits/approvals count as "edit" and template creation counts as "create", while view/export stay ungated. I'm weighing whether to touch asset-gate.ts directly or just consume its existing canAsset helper, leaning toward adding a minimal constant there since the instructions seem to expect some modification to that file.

I decide to append a small exported mapping to asset-gate.ts that links each Model Studio editor action to its corresponding asset op, keeping it at the end of the file to avoid merge conflicts, then plan to cover it with tests. Moving on to the server service file, I note it imports the StudioStore type only and start sketching a `resolveModels` function that processes rows per asset.

Then I lay out the plan for `loadModel`, which gates view access and ownership before returning the doc, head revision, and edit permission, followed by `saveModelRevision`, which gates edit access, validates ownership, parses the untrusted document with a zod schema, runs validation and conversion to RigSpec, checks the compiled creature for namespace and skin quality, verifies the head isn't stale, and updates the manifest with the canonical spec hash and compiled model hash.

I'm also adding the model doc asset entry with its own path and provenance (generator, doc, spec, compiler, hashes, stats, quality, warnings, basedOn), enforcing that the asset key must match the doc's internal name since renames aren't allowed in v1. Then I sketch a `DraftStore` interface with get/put/delete methods and a simple in-memory implementation, noting that real wiring isn't done yet so the API should return a 503 for drafts in this phase.

I define a pure autosave scheduling function that decides whether an autosave is due based on idle time and maximum elapsed time since the first dirty edit, and confirm it's tested. Then I'm planning the HTTP handlers file, reusing shared framework-free utilities from the studios module, and outlining the endpoints for listing models, fetching a single model doc with validation/access info, and saving via POST.

I also need GET/PUT draft endpoints returning 503 when no draft store exists, and I'm weighing how to gate the editor's visibility behind the `cyrus_model_editor_enabled` setting -- deciding to require the flag on for everyone, with a non-production dev override via env var for devhost screenshots, since setting env on devhost isn't the same as flipping a flag in production.

For the page itself, `app/dashboard/cyrus/[id]/studio/model-editor/page.tsx` resolves studio context and checks the flag, then the client fetches the project and models through a single endpoint keyed by root build id, returning project info, access, model list, and head revision id. I'm planning the route structure for `app/api/cyrus/assets/v1/model-editor/route.ts` and its nested routes...

I'm reusing the existing studio dependency helpers for store, plan, and chain, layering in a drafts stub and a flag check via the host settings, so visibility combines studio access with the feature flag. I'll put this editor-specific deps module under `lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/deps.ts`, importing from the sibling studios deps and the host module to keep the seam clean.

For narrow viewports I'm designing a read-only approve flow: below 760px it shows a turntable render you can drag to orbit, a computed diff of changes against the saved revision, budget/check summaries, and Approve/Reject actions that map to saving or discarding the draft, with locked plans restricted to view-only. The main ModelEditor component will be sizeable, composed of an outliner, a viewport adapter, a tabbed inspector for cubes/keyframes/checks, UV and budget panels, a timeline, and a candidate bar whose AI-edit hooks exist in the UI but aren't yet wired to actual model calls.

The prompt dock will call an injected `onPrompt` hook on submit, defaulting to a toast saying model edits aren't connected yet; I'm also considering a dev-only deterministic fake candidate generator, gated behind a query flag and non-production check, purely to help demo the merge UI for screenshots. For the viewport itself, I'm sketching an internal software renderer that projects cube faces as quads using world matrices from each pose, sorts them by depth painter's-style, and flat-shades each face using palette colors.

Since canvas 2D texture mapping is too complex for now, I'll use flat material colors per face with simple directional lighting instead, leaving real texture rendering for when the three.js viewport lands later. I'm also planning the gizmo interactions—axis-arrow dragging for movement, horizontal drag for rotation, polygon hit-testing for picking, orbit controls via right-drag, wheel zoom, a grid floor, and a bones overlay showing pivot points and connecting lines.

I need a ViewportAdapter interface that different renderers (canvas now, three.js later) can implement, built around a pure `buildScene` function that converts the document and pose into a renderable scene graph of boxes and bones with world-space geometry, keeping the math testable and renderer-agnostic.

The pose computation applies each bone's local transform as pivot-centered rotation and scale combined with animated translation, then composes with the parent's world matrix to get world-space positions, with cube points transformed directly by their bone's world matrix. I'll reuse the container query approach from .cyrus-root for my own `me-` prefixed classes within `.cys`, confirming the studio page already sits inside the cyrus layout wrapper. Now I'm planning the component structure, starting with a viewport adapter module under the editor folder.

For ModelEditor's state, I'm sketching out the data shape covering the model view, op log, selection, active tool, snap settings, playback clip/time, camera orbit state, inspector tabs, visibility toggles, merge candidate for conflict resolution, prompt text, and save/unsaved tracking—mirroring the same workspace/narrow dual-render pattern via CSS container queries used in the texture studio. I'm also outlining the CanvasViewport component's props: scene, camera, selection, tool, and pick/drag callbacks.

For the drag interaction, I'm planning pointer handling: hit-testing gizmo axis handles to start an axis drag, otherwise selecting the cube or starting an orbit; on move, converting pixel deltas into move/resize/pivot/rotate ops with snapping and firing a preview callback; on release, committing the op to the log; and right-drag or empty-space drag rotating the camera orbit.

Now I'm sketching the renderer: capping device pixel ratio, drawing a background floor grid, then shading each face using a fixed world light direction dotted with the face normal, with selected cube faces getting a violet outline and others thin dark edges, wireframe mode skipping fills, and a bones overlay drawing pivot dots and connecting lines with the selected bone highlighted.

I'm then figuring out the gizmo at the active pivot, drawing three axis arrows scaled so their screen projection stays around 48px regardless of zoom, with resize handles getting square tips and rotation shown via arc/ring glyphs that let dragging convert horizontal pixel movement into rotation about that axis. Finally I'm connecting the pose rendering to the current clip and time from the timeline.

For the timeline itself, I'm working through clip tabs, playback controls, and a "Key" button that inserts a keyframe for the selected bone's rotation at the current time using its sampled or manually-set value. Each track row shows diamond-shaped key markers positioned by time, with wave tracks rendered as sine curves, and I'm wiring up selection, scrubbing via the playhead, and horizontal dragging to move keys.

Now I'm fleshing out the Keyframe inspector tab -- showing time/value/ease fields and a delete option for a selected key, or a quick "set key" prompt when none is selected, plus clip-level settings like length and loop. For the Cube inspector tab, I'm defining what shows for a selected bone (name, parent, pivot, rotation, tag) versus a selected cube, which adds a CUBE section with from/to coordinates, size, inflate, and material options.

I'm also sketching rotation and pivot fields with editor warnings for Minecraft constraints, a UV BOX section that renders the texture sheet with cube nets and auto-pack or pinned placement options, a Checks tab showing validation verdicts and budgets, and the left/center layout with an outliner tree, toolbar actions, and the main viewport with its tool rail and view controls.

For the right side I'm thinking through inspector tabs, and for narrow screens a condensed card view showing model status, a read-only turntable preview, a diff of what changed, and approve/reject controls that respect edit permissions. I'm also working out how a locked plan should behave -- likely rendering the full editor in read-only mode with a lock banner rather than hiding it entirely.

For the prompt dock, since no model is actually connected yet, I'm planning for submission to either generate a fake candidate when a dev flag is enabled or show a toast explaining nothing was sent. For persistence I'm designing autosave to hit the server draft endpoint with a localStorage fallback, plus a restore banner when an unsaved draft differs from the base, and a save-revision flow that posts the document along with the base asset id and expected head for concurrency control.

On success it rebases the log, updates the base asset and head pointers, and toasts the new revision number; a 409 conflict toasts a stale-save error. I'm also mapping out keyboard shortcuts for tools, mirroring, undo/redo, delete, duplicate, hide, and play, and splitting this large component into separate files for state/layout, the side panels, and the canvas viewport adapter, while checking which icon set is actually available to use.

Since the existing icon library doesn't cover transform-specific icons like move, rotate, resize, pivot, or bone, I'll build a small local icon set with consistent inline SVG styling in its own file. I'm also noting the avatar icon source for candidates, deciding to skip token estimates since there's no AI integration yet and just show a hint instead, and checking which CSS variables are available for styling.

Now I'll start writing the viewport adapter.

Now I'm reasoning through gizmo placement: since the scene can be posed (bone transforms applied) while edits happen in rest coordinates, dragging along a world axis won't perfectly match the rest-space axis for rotated bones — I'm accepting this as an approximation rather than solving full inverse kinematics. I'm deciding the viewport should only show posed positions when a "Pose" toggle is enabled, defaulting to rest pose otherwise so editing tools behave predictably.

I'm wiring up the commit pipeline so operations log their application, update selection state, and surface a toast error if the user's plan is read-only, plus sketching a numeric inspector field that commits edits on blur or enter.

For the timeline I'm laying out track rows with percentage-positioned key diamonds, a cyan playhead driven by a requestAnimationFrame loop, and click-to-seek on the ruler, looping playback based on the clip's loop flag. The UV sheet panel renders each box's faces with shaded material colors, highlighting the selected box and dashing pinned ones, with drag-to-reposition snapping to integer pixels and emitting a setUv operation on release.

For the candidate bar I'm showing the pending edit's origin and change count with an overlap tag, plus Compare, Apply, and Reject actions—Apply merges base/ours/theirs with accept/resolve choices and commits a replace operation labeled "Accept Cyrus edit." The prompt dock handles sending a prompt either to a fake candidate generator in dev mode or shows a toast that the model isn't connected yet, alongside route and model chips.

Now I'm thinking through the narrow turntable view: a separate component sharing state with its own orbit camera, a "What changed" summary diffing saved vs current doc (or showing the candidate diff if pending), budget display, and Reject/Approve actions that either rebase to saved doc or save with an approve action, disabled when read-only or unchanged. I also need theme detection via a MutationObserver watching the document's data-theme attribute, global keyboard shortcuts when no input is focused, and an autosave effect that computes a canonical JSON hash to detect real changes.

I'm wiring up a per-document autosave timer: on firing, it tries the draft API endpoint and falls back to localStorage on failure, then updates a status indicator showing when the draft was last saved. I'll start writing panels.tsx first, then move on to ModelEditor.tsx.

3	// real path will: it takes the BASE revision's RigSpec (never the working copy), edits the spec, re-validates it and
4	// lines it up with the base (fromRigSpec like), so its ids match R. Pure + client-safe.
5	import { checkRigSpec } from "../../creature/spec";
6	import { boneByName, type ModelDoc } from "./doc";
7	import { fromRigSpec, toRigSpec } from "./rigspec";
8	
9	type SpecBone = { name: string; cubes: { from: number[]; to: number[] }[] };
10	type SpecClip = { tracks: { bone: string; channel: string; wave?: { amp: number[] }; keys?: { v: number[] }[] }[] };
11	
12	/** "make the hood longer ..." -> lengthen the named bone's first cube by 2 units downward and widen its idle sway. */
13	export function fakeModelCandidate(base: ModelDoc, prompt: string): { ok: true; doc: ModelDoc; summary: string } | { ok: false; error: string } {
14	  const spec = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(toRigSpec(base).spec)) as Record<string, unknown> & { bones: SpecBone[]; animations: Record<string, SpecClip> };
15	  const words = prompt.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z_]+/g) ?? [];
16	  const target = spec.bones.find((b) => words.includes(b.name) && b.cubes.length) ?? spec.bones.find((b) => b.cubes.length && boneByName(base, b.name)?.parent !== null);
17	  if (!target) return { ok: false, error: "nothing to edit" };
18	  const c = target.cubes[0];
19	  c.from[1] = Math.max(-63, c.from[1] - 2);
20	  for (const t of spec.animations.idle?.tracks ?? []) if (t.bone === target.name && t.channel === "rotation") {
21	    if (t.wave) t.wave.amp = t.wave.amp.map((v) => Math.max(-180, Math.min(180, Math.round(v * 1.5 * 100) / 100)));
22	    else for (const k of t.keys ?? []) k.v = k.v.map((v) => Math.round(v * 1.5 * 100) / 100);
</system-reminder>

cat >> /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r17/docs/DOCUMENTATION.md <<'EOF'

## Cyrus Model Studio: cuboid and bone editor (layer 2, 2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r17-editor`, NOT deployed, flag OFF)

Our OWN cuboid + bone editor for RigSpec creatures (plan: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md` sections 2-3, 6; mockup `model-editor.html`, NOT owner-reviewed yet). Blockbench is GPL-3: nothing of it is embedded, copied or read; the document model, ops, merge rule and renderer are written from scratch. Layer 1 (three.js viewport + paint) is a separate branch (`feature/cyrus-r16-viewport`, uncommitted when this landed), so the editor draws through a thin adapter with an internal GPU-free canvas renderer until that viewport merges.

### 1. Pure core (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/`, client-safe, no GPU, no `node:` in the client graph)
| File | What |
|---|---|
| `doc.ts` | `ModelDoc` v1 (mime `application/vnd.cyrus.modeldoc+json`): bones (id, name, parent id, pivot, rotation, tag, hide/lock), cubes (id, bone, from/to = origin + size, editor-only rotation + pivot + label, inflate, material/shade/fadeTo, texture slot, UV pin, decals), clips (tracks of keys with ids, or waves), texture slots, an id counter `seq` (replay gives the same ids). Zod parser for untrusted docs (`checkModelDoc`, 256 KB cap). |
| `rigspec.ts` | `fromRigSpec(spec, { like })` / `toRigSpec(doc)`. `like` lines a RigSpec (an AI candidate) up with a base doc: bones by name, cubes by identical from/to/material then by position, keys by (clip, bone, channel, t). `toRigSpec` reports editor-only fields it drops (cube rotation, UV pins, extra texture slots). |
| `ops.ts` | The v1 operations (plan section 3): add bone/cube, delete (subtree + its tracks), duplicate, mirror X (`_l`/`_r`, also mirrors decals and animation tracks), move/rotate/resize/scale with snapping (1 unit = 1/16 block grid; angle snaps), reparent (cycle-safe), pivot, UV pin/auto, rename, hide/lock, group, material/shade/inflate/tag, palette, clips + keys (set/delete/move/ease, wave -> keys, loop seam kept), `replace` (an accepted AI merge or a restored draft = one step). Locked nodes refuse edits. Ops never mutate their input. |
| `history.ts` | Undo/redo as an OP LOG `{ base, entries, at }` with a per-step cache; `replay(base, ops)` rebuilds any step from the base (tested byte-equal to the cache); 200 steps max (older ones fold into the base). |
| `validate.ts` | Structured issues `{ code, severity, path, node?, message }`: structure (ids, one root, parents, cycles, orphans), names/paths (bone/clip/model names, safe `assets/...png` slot paths), the RigSpec caps (constants from `creature/spec.ts`), the target profile (`profiles.ts`), the UV layout, then the authoritative `checkRigSpec` on `toRigSpec(doc)` with errors mapped back to the bone/cube. Live budgets for the panel. |
| `uv.ts` | Box-UV layout: auto boxes use exactly the compiler's shelf packer (rig-c1; test: same rectangles as `layoutSkin`), pinned boxes are placed first and auto ones flow around them. Pins are editor-only until RigSpec v1.1 / rig-c2 (warning `uv_pin_editor_only`). |
| `pose.ts`, `scene.ts` | Deterministic sampler (= `compile.ts sampleTrack`, tested), bone/cube world matrices (= `preview.ts poseMatrices`, tested), posed scene faces, camera projection, picking, gizmo axis drag maths. |
| `merge.ts` | The AI-edit merge rule: 3-way per node id (bone, cube, key, clip, track, palette colour, meta), field by field; a cube's box (from/to/pivot) is ONE field. One side changed -> that side; both changed differently -> an OVERLAP, human wins by default, `resolve` picks Cyrus per overlap; `accept` = Apply part. Cyrus's new ids are renumbered past both counters; a clashing new bone name is renamed for Cyrus's side; nodes left hanging are dropped with a note. |
| `gate.ts` | `canModelEditor(plan, action)`; the action -> asset-op map is `MODEL_EDITOR_ACTION_OP` in `engine-core/asset-gate.ts` (view/export never gated; edit, autosave, save, approve, ai_edit = edit; create = create). Top plan only, unknown plan fails closed for edits. (Layer 1 adds its own `MODEL_STUDIO_OP` map in the same file; unify them when both are merged.) |
| `autosave.ts` | Schedule: 5 s after the last edit, at most 30 s after the first unsaved edit. |
| `fake-candidate.ts` | A deterministic stand-in for an AI edit (base revision's RigSpec -> edit -> checkRigSpec -> `fromRigSpec like`). Used by tests and by `?fakeCandidate=1` outside production. NO model call anywhere. |

### 2. Exporters (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/export/`, server only)
Game-neutral `ModelExporter { id, game, target, formats, maturity, unverified, run(doc, ctx) }`; `runExport` refuses maturity `planned` unless `allowPlanned` (tests/devhost only). Export is never plan-gated.
- `minecraft-bbmodel` (beta): `toRigSpec` -> `checkReturnedCreature` (re-validate, rig-c1 compile, skin quality) -> the creature JSON, `.bbmodel`, skin PNG. Byte-identical to what a build writes (tested).
- `hytale-blockymodel-draft` (**planned**, never offered to customers): uses ONLY the VERIFIED facts of `N-hytale.md` (V1 `.blockymodel`/`.blockyanim` + PNG, V2 cuboids/quads only + fixed materials, V3 64 px per block for mobs/equipment, 32 for blocks: the skin is upscaled 4x). Every other choice is listed as UNVERIFIED (`HYTALE_UNVERIFIED`, U1-U16: JSON layout and key names, units, node origins, quaternion order, face names and mapping, textureLayout, inflate as stretch, glow as fullbright, folder layout/no manifest, .blockyanim layout and 60 fps frames, delta semantics, scale tracks dropped, max texture size, clip-name mapping, baked waves). A sidecar `cyrus-export.json` says `loadedByRealClient: false`. Golden: `test/fixtures/cyrus-modelstudio/banshee.hytale-draft.golden.json` (regenerate only on a deliberate change: `UPDATE_MODELSTUDIO_GOLDEN=1`).

### 3. Save path (`service.ts`, `http.ts`, `deps.ts`; routes under `/api/cyrus/assets/v1/model-editor`)
- A mod's model = the newest `CyrusProjectAsset` of kind `model` for its key: a build's RigSpec row (`RIG_SPEC_MIME`) is converted, an editor row (`MODEL_DOC_MIME`) is read as is.
- Save revision (`POST .../model-editor/:projectId/:key`): gate (server side, fail closed) -> ownership -> parse -> validate (errors = 422 with issues) -> `checkReturnedCreature` (compile + skin quality, 422 if it fails) -> `expectedHeadId` (409 `stale_head`) -> NEW revision kind `asset` (manifest: `assets/creatures/<name>.json`, `bettermodel/<key>.bbmodel`, `assets/models/<name>.modeldoc.json`) + a new asset row (origin `edited`, provenance = doc + explicit RigSpec + hashes). Drafts are cleared.

content.thinking:
I'm trying to pin down which assertion is failing — possibly a floating-point boundary issue where accumulated values land just inside or outside the epsilon tolerance near a tick threshold.

I think the actual bug is in how cycle ranges are computed: using floor division on `from`/`to` without an epsilon can cause an instant exactly at a tick boundary (within floating error) to be excluded in one tick window but never caught in the adjacent one, effectively dropping it. The fix is to compute `endCycle` as `floor((to + eps) / L)` so near-boundary instants get included consistently across both tick windows.

input.command:
cd /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r17 && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/DOCUMENTATION.md'
s=open(p).read()
anchor='### 2. Exporters (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/export/`, server only)'
add='''### 1b. Timeline core (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/timeline/`, GAME-NEUTRAL, owner decision 2026-10-10)
Motion, animation and effects are a foundational, game-agnostic part of Cyrus (walk cycles, gun cock/fire/reload, car doors + a character getting in, explosions, fire, water), playable live in the studios and tied to the texture and sound studios. The timeline core is therefore its own folder with no Minecraft/RigSpec assumptions (game specifics live in `rigspec.ts` and the exporters); a later Motion core (EffectSpec ...) builds on these types.
- `types.ts`: `Clip { name, length (seconds), loop, tracks, events? }`, keys/events at NORMALISED time `t` 0..1. Tracks carry a typed `kind`: `transform` (bone/node rotation, position, scale; keys or a seamless wave) is implemented and stored in ModelDoc v1; `sound_cue`, `particle`, `light`, `material`, `state` are declared extension points (`TRACK_KINDS` status `planned`: shapes fixed and sampled, not stored in ModelDoc v1, not exported). `ClipEvent { id, t, name, data? }` = clip metadata "events at times" (stored; ops `setEvent` / `deleteEvent`; merged per id; editor-only for RigSpec v1 with warning `clip_events_editor_only`).
- `sampler.ts`: ONE deterministic sampler: `sampleClip(clip, time)` -> node transforms, scalar channels, machine states; `firedBetween(clip, from, to)` -> every instant (events, cues, bursts, state changes) crossed, half-open and wrap-aware (float drift at a wrap cannot drop an instant). Transform maths == `creature/compile.ts sampleTrack` (tested on every fixture track); `pose.ts` uses it.
- `clock.ts`: the playback API a viewport or a live simulation drives: `clockInit / Load / Play / Pause / Toggle / Scrub / Speed (0.1-4x) / Loop`, `clockTick(clock, dt, clip)` -> new state + fired instants + wraps + ended. Pure (the host feeds elapsed seconds). The editor's play button, speed select and the "event <name>" flash run on it.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-modelstudio-timeline.test.ts`.

'''
s=s.replace(anchor, add+anchor)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "1b. Timeline core" docs/DOCUMENTATION.md

input.message:
Model Studio layer 2 is built on `feature/cyrus-r17-editor` (worktree /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r17, head 1edc88f7a8). It is not deployed. One new setting, `cyrus_model_editor_enabled`, defaults OFF, and the page and API return 404 while it is off. No migration.

- **Core (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/`):** all of it is our own code and runs in the browser. It has the document model, the v1 operations, undo as an op log that replays the same way every time, checks that point to the bone or cube at fault, and the 3-way merge for AI edits. Loading a RigSpec and saving it back gives byte-identical .bbmodel and skin output. The plan gate is added to `asset-gate.ts`.
- **Your timeline request:** `editor/timeline/` is game-neutral. Tracks have a typed kind: transform works now; sound cue, particle, light, material and state-machine are declared but not stored yet. Clips can carry events at set times. There is one deterministic sampler and a play/pause/scrub/loop/speed clock that drives the editor.
- **Hytale exporter:** a draft at maturity "planned", never shown to customers. It uses only 3 verified facts; 16 format guesses are labelled unverified and pinned by a golden test.
- **UI and saving:** the page is at `/studio/model-editor`, in dark, light and a read-only phone approve view. Saves go through the existing revision store with autosave.

**Ran:** 70 new tests; full suite 1706/1707. The one failure, `cyrus-admin.test.ts`, crashed only in the loaded full run and passes alone (31/31). tsc is clean. 8 screenshots, including a real save on devhost.

**Not run:** no real Minecraft or Hytale client, no real AI calls.

**Open:** the next build overwrites editor saves; there is no server draft table yet; layer 1 (r16) is not in r2, so the 3D view is a stand-in.
